newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel warns PLO against declaring state.
newsitem.headline: Israel warns PLO against declaring state.

text.p: Israel warned Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Sunday that a unilateral declaration of a Palestinian state would be a "serious mistake".

"Declaration of a state from the Palestinian side...would of course be a very serious violation of agreements signed between them and the government of Israel," Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh told Israel radio.
"All I can say is Israel is certainly prepared for this occurrence and it would be a serious mistake by the Palestinian side."

Naveh was responding to a warning by Arafat on Saturday that he could declare Palestinian independence in reaction to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to build a new neighbourhood for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem.

"We are supposed to declare the setting up of a Palestinian state in five years but what would happen if I declare it right here? What would he (Netanyahu) do then? It's tit-for-tat and we have our weapons too," Arafat told an emergency session of the Cairo-based Arab League.

Israel's approval on Wednesday of a plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews in Jabal Abu Ghneim, a tree-lined hill in Arab East Jerusalem called Har Homa by Israel, sparked international criticism and Palestinian warnings it could unleash bloodshed.
Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Sunday that, for now, Arafat was preventing an outburst of violence.
"The Palestinian Authority has made every effort not to come into direct confrontation (with Israel)," said Mordechai in remarks broadcast on Israel's army radio.
"Nobody knows what will happen when the tractors begin working at Har Homa or when Arafat concludes after his visit in Washington that doesn't serve all his interests," he said.
Arafat is to meet U.S. President Bill Clinton in Washington on Monday.

Under a deal in which Israel handed 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule in January, Israel committed to a timetable of three more withdrawals from rural areas of the West Bank of undetermined size.
The first of the pullbacks is to be by March 7.
Netanyahu's office said on Sunday that the government would meet on March 6, to vote on the pullback.
"Immediately after the cabinet decides it will be implemented," a Netanyahu spokesman said.

Israel captured East Jerusalem along with the rest of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip in the 1967 Middle East war. In a move not recognised by the international community it annexed East Jerusalem, declaring it part of an indivisible capital.
The Palestinians want to establish an independent state in the territories with East Jerusalem as capital. According to interim peace deals, the sides are to reach a final peace accord in 1999.
